translation_notes: The 8-way if/elif choosing a predicate by note_type collapses to one `+{ {concept} ?p ?o }` inside `for @bindings in (...)`, with predicate and object supplied per row by a Python dict lookup (_NOTE_PREDICATES) that mirrors the original dispatch, defaulting to skos:note exactly like the original `else` branch.

Wrapped the extracted statement in graph_construct_qs_notes(obj, concept, g) to restore the obj/concept/g bindings the enclosing `for obj in results:` loop supplies in the source file (this region is one of the ones without a directly visible graph).
Only add_in_loop's construction is credited here; the coercion_datatype stratum tag on this region concerns a different line (158, the Literal(...) with lang=), not this triple pattern.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the eight-branch if/elif chain, which differs only by the SKOS predicate, becomes one add whose predicate is `SKOS[note.note_type if note.note_type in note_types else "note"]` (the note types are exactly the SKOS local names, and every other value falls back to skos:note as the original `else` does); the redundant guard `if obj.has_notes.all():` is dropped.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the add is `+{ {concept} skos:{...} f"{note.name}"@{note.language} }` -- a prefixed name with a computed local part and a language literal with an interpolated tag; it needs its own `@prefix skos:` (translated.ldpy declared none and kept SKOS as a Python Namespace in a lookup table) and `@graph g`.

The language literal is not exactly Literal(name, lang=language): a None tag raises TypeError in the island where rdflib gives a plain literal. The repository's SkosNote.language is a non-null CharField, so None cannot occur; an empty string gives a plain literal on both sides.
No exception to the symmetry rule. Most of the gain is the rereading (care 0.34): the notation adds little once the dispatch is a single add.
